test_title: RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I Official Paper (Held On: 23 Jun, 2025 Shift 3)
subject: general
question: At what rate (in percentage) per annum will ₹1,400 give ₹700 as simple interest in 5 years?
solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Total Interest Percentage = (**Interest** ÷ **Principal**) × 100

Total Interest % = (700 ÷ 1400) × 100 = **50%**

**Rate of Interest** per annum = Total Interest % ÷ **Time**

**Rate (R)** = 50% ÷ 5 = **10%**

**∴ The correct answer is 10%.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

**Principal (P)** = ₹1,400

**Simple Interest (SI)** = ₹700

**Time (T)** = 5 years

**Formula Used:**

SI = (P × R × T) ÷ 100

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/d59ee355bd30b5b4aa55f613ebf5ce847f12de171197b9e46433adf50ba61ec4.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ 700 = (1400 × R × 5) ÷ 100

⇒ 700 = 14 × R × 5

⇒ 700 = 70 × R

⇒ R = 700 ÷ 70

⇒ R = 10%

**∴ The correct answer is 10%.**

**__Additional Information__**

Simple Interest (SI)

It is the interest calculated only on the initial **Principal** amount for the entire period. Formula: SI = (P × R × T) ÷ 100.

Amount (A)

The total money (Principal + Interest) to be paid back after the time period. Formula: A = P + SI = P(1 + RT ÷ 100).

Rate of Interest (R)

The percentage of the **Principal** charged as interest per year. R = (SI × 100) ÷ (P × T).
